DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph 10 February 2021 MR. ROGELIO R. MERIDA Chairman Municipal Agriculture and Fisheries Council Municipality of Magdiwang, Province of Romblon Dear Mr. Merida: This is in reference to your letter dated 9 December 2019 requesting this Department's opinion and guidance concerning the action of the Sangguniang Bayan of Magdiwang, Province of Romblon of intending to form a local water district. Per your subject letter, the herein concerned Municipality adopted Resolution No. 19-155 dated 6 September 2019, entitled "A Resolution Requesting the Local Water Utilities Administration for the Formation of a Water District in the Municipality of Magdiwang, Province of Romblon" pursuant to Presidential Decree No. 198 (Provincial Water Utilities Act of 1973), as amended. In essence, said Resolution pursues the formation of a local Water District and subsequently transfer to it all local waterworks facilities and properties owned by the Municipality of Magdiwang, Romblon. In opposition to the aforesaid Resolution, the Municipal Development Council (MDC) passed MDC Resolution No. 2019-14, dated 6 November 2019, entitled "Strong Opposition to Municipal Resolution No. 19-155, entitled: Requesting the Local Water Utilities Administration (LWUA) for the Formation of a Water District in the Municipality of Magdiwang, Romblon". The MDC's remonstrations can be reduced to the following essential arguments, thus: 1. The subject Resolution lacks essential requisites of a valid Resolution pursuant to Section 6 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 198, as amended;

2. The subject Resolution is unilateral and was passed without due regard to prior study, consultation and public hearing; 3. The subject Resolution is highly immoral and illegal because its intentions are to cause damage and undue injury to the local government and to give undue advantage and benefits to some individuals in the Water District intended to be formed, to the prejudice of the consuming public and the public interests. At the outset, P.D. No. 198, series of 1973 authorizes the legislative body of any city, municipality or province to form and create their respective water districts through a resolution passed by the Sangguniang. The same Decree provides that: Local water districts may be formed pursuant to this Title for the purposes of (a) acquirinq. installing. improving. maintaininq and operatina water supply and distribution systems for domestic. industrial, municipal and agricultural uses for residents and lands within the boundaries of such districts. (b) providing, maintaining and operating wate-water collection. treatment and disposal facilities. and (c) conductina such other functions and operations incidental to water resource development. utilization and disposal within such districts. as are necessary or incidental to said purpose. (Emphasis supplied) Furthermore, the said Decree prescribes the essential requisites of a valid resolution for purposes of forming a water district. Specifically, Section 6 thereof reads: "Section 6. Formation of District. - This Act is the source of authorization and power to form and maintain a district. Once formed, a district is subject to the provisions of this Act and not under the jurisdiction of any political subdivision. To form a district, the legislative body of any city, municipality or province shall enact a resolution containing the following: (a) The name of the local water district, which shall include the name of the city, municipality, or province, or region thereof, served by said system, followed by the words "Water District". (b) A description of the boundary of the district. In the case of a city or municipality, such boundary may include all lands within the city or municipality. A district may include one or more municipalities, cities or provinces, or portions thereof. (c) A statement of intent to transfer any and all waterworks and/or sewerage facilities owned by such city, municipality or

province to such district pursuant to a contract authorized by Section 31 (b) of this Title. (d) A statement identifying the purpose for which the district is formed, which shall include those purposes outlined in Section 5 above. (e) The names of the initial directors of the district with the date of expiration of term of office for each. (f) A statement that the district may only be dissolved on the grounds and under the conditions set forth in Section 44 of this Title. (g) A statement acknowledging the powers, rights and obligations as set forth in Section 36 of this Title. Nothing in the resolution of formation shall state or infer that the local legislative body has the power to dissolve, alter or affect the district beyond that specifically provided for in this Act. If two or more cities, municipalities or provinces, or any combination thereof, desire to form a single district, a similar resolution shall be adopted in each city, municipality and province." Perusal of the subject Resolution in question, the same appears to be LQt compliant with the essential requisites prescribed under PD No. 198, as above-cited. Moreover, it bears noting that PD No. 198 defines "Local water districts", viz: "Local Water Utility. Any district, city, municipality, province, investor-owned public utility or cooperative corporation which owns or operates a water system serving an urban center in the Philippines, except that said term shall not included the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) or any system operated by the Bureau of Public Work as successor to the Wells and Springs Department of the National Waterworks and Sewerage Authority." (Emphasis supplied) As can be clearly gleaned from the foregoing, the formation of water district is applicable only to those city, municipality, province, who owns or operates a water system serving an urban center in the Philippines. Accordingly, we are constrained to concur with the position of MDC that herein concerned Municipality is not qualified to form a water district pursuant to PD No. 198, as amended. As represented in the subject letter,

herein concemed Municipality has a population of less than 20,000 people. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
